policy_name: Use of enterprise Generative AI tools in the Victorian public sector
issuing_authority: Office of the Victorian Information Commissioner (OVIC)
regulatory_regime: Privacy and Data Protection Act 2014 (Vic) – Information Privacy Principles and Victorian Protective Data Security Standards (regulator guidance)
geo_constraints: Victorian public sector organisations subject to Parts 3 and 4 of the Privacy and Data Protection Act 2014

locale_context.regulation: Regulator guidance · minimum expectations under privacy and data-security law
locale_context.culture: Victorian information-regulator guidance: frames enterprise GenAI adoption through existing statutory privacy principles and protective security standards, stressing that organisations stay accountable for AI output ('cannot simply say … caused by AI').

collection, use and disclosure of personal information via Generative AI

conditions: information privacy section applies to organisations covered by Part 3 of the PDP Act
minimum expectations to work through prior to purchasing and integrating an enterprise Generative AI tool
objective: Set out OVIC's minimum expectations and the key information privacy and security obligations for Victorian public sector organisations adopting enterprise Generative AI tools.

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/ovic.docx). Date 'March 2025' from the document footer; exact day unknown. No official URL for this document is printed (only OVIC resource links in footnotes), so source_uri points to the asago copy. Status 'voluntary': the guidance states minimum expectations (SHOULD) but restates mandatory statutory duties under the PDP Act. Not verified whether this is the latest version.

clauses.original_text: Undertake privacy impact assessments (PIAs) to understand the ways in which the enterprise Generative AI tool will be utilised, the risks it presents to the privacy of individuals, whether and how those risks can be mitigated, and in light of any residual risks, the extent to which it is appropriate to proceed to purchase the tool.
clauses.requirement: conduct PIAs (per function or business unit) before purchasing an enterprise Generative AI tool and regularly review risks and controls
clauses.condition: prior to purchasing and integrating an enterprise Generative AI tool
clauses.purpose: protect individuals' privacy; decide whether to proceed
clauses.applicable_systems: enterprise Generative AI tools (e.g. tenanted Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the .docx (pandoc text); footnote markers removed. Footnote 7: one overarching PIA is likely insufficient; PIAs should be per function or business unit.

clauses.original_text: Ensure that enterprise Generative AI tools are not used to make decisions, undertake assessments, or for other administrative functions that may have consequences for individuals or cause them significant harm.
clauses.object: enterprise Generative AI tools for consequential decisions or assessments
clauses.requirement: prevent use of enterprise Generative AI to make decisions or assessments with consequences for individuals
clauses.purpose: avoid unfair decisions based on inaccurate or diminished-quality AI-generated information
clauses.applicable_systems: enterprise Generative AI tools (e.g. tenanted Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the .docx (pandoc text); footnote markers removed.

clauses.original_text: Ensure that settings can be configured to enhance information privacy and information security, such as disabling or limiting data sharing between certain platforms and between the VPS organisation and the company that owns the enterprise Generative AI tool.
clauses.object: data sharing settings of enterprise Generative AI tools
clauses.requirement: configure the tool to limit data sharing between platforms and with the vendor
clauses.applicable_systems: enterprise Generative AI tools (e.g. tenanted Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the .docx (pandoc text); footnote markers removed.

clauses.original_text: Develop and implement clear and tailored guidance and training for their staff, contracted service providers and other personnel on the use of the enterprise Generative AI tool, that: covers how to safely and responsibly use the enterprise Generative AI tool, prompt engineering, risk assessment and management, human review of generated outputs, and active monitoring and reviews to identify potential misuse ensures all users of the enterprise Generative AI tool are aware of and understand what information they are permitted to enter into the enterprise Generative AI tool and its permitted use cases
clauses.object: use of the enterprise Generative AI tool
clauses.recipient: staff, contracted service providers and other personnel
clauses.requirement: train users on safe use, human review of outputs, permitted inputs and permitted use cases
clauses.purpose: safe and responsible use; prevent misuse and inaccurate outputs
clauses.applicable_systems: enterprise Generative AI tools (e.g. tenanted Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the .docx (pandoc text); footnote markers removed. Nested bullets flattened; a third bullet (awareness of how the tool handles personal information and ensuring accuracy) omitted.

clauses.original_text: Develop an incident response plan for dealing with inadvertent or unauthorised disclosures, access or misuse of information through the enterprise Generative AI tool. VPS organisations are responsible for all actions and content generated by the enterprise Generative AI tool they use. Where an information security incident or interference with privacy occurs through the use of the tool, VPS organisations will not be able to simply say that the incident or interference was caused by AI. Notify OVIC of information privacy and information security incidents, in line with the Information Security Incident Notification Scheme.
clauses.object: information privacy and security incidents involving the tool
clauses.requirement: maintain an AI incident response plan, accept responsibility for AI-generated content and notify OVIC of incidents
clauses.applicable_systems: enterprise Generative AI tools (e.g. tenanted Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the .docx (pandoc text); footnote markers removed. Two consecutive bullets combined.

clauses.original_text: Before VPS organisations implement any enterprise Generative AI tool, the public sector body head must assess the information security risks to the confidentiality, integrity and availability of public sector information and systems proposed to be used by the enterprise Generative AI tool, and ensure adherence to the Victorian Protective Data Security Standards (the Standards).
clauses.object: information security risks of the enterprise Generative AI tool
clauses.recipient: contracted service providers (via the security risk assessment)
clauses.requirement: assess confidentiality, integrity and availability risks and comply with the VPDSS before implementation, including evaluation of relevant contracted service providers
clauses.condition: before implementing any enterprise Generative AI tool
clauses.purpose: protect public sector information and systems
clauses.applicable_systems: enterprise Generative AI tools (e.g. tenanted Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the .docx (pandoc text); footnote markers removed. This restates statutory obligations under Part 4 of the Privacy and Data Protection Act 2014 (hence MUST); the guidance itself is not binding.
